summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with HCV-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for observation following radiofrequency ablation of liver lesions in segments 8 and 5, along with therapeutic drainage of 5 liters of ascites. The procedure was performed under general anesthesia and was uncomplicated, though the initial ascitic fluid was slightly bloody, prompting overnight monitoring. Serial hemoglobin and hematocrit levels remained stable, and mild hyponatremia (Na 130) was managed with albumin infusion. The patient’s pain was controlled with oxycodone, and he remained hemodynamically stable throughout. He was discharged home with instructions to continue home medications, use oxycodone as needed for pain, and follow up with his primary care provider for repeat labs and hepatology for a CT scan in four weeks.
